references.text: Isaiah describes a similar spiritual phenomenon where people hear but do not understand, and see but do not perceive, as a judgment on their own blindness, which Jesus refers to in his statement that those who see will become blind.

Jesus quoted directly from Isaiah to explain why he spoke in parables: so that those who see may not see, and those who hear may not understand, a direct parallel to the judgment against the self-righteous in John 9.

Paul quoted the same passage from Isaiah to describe how the gospel becomes a scent of death for those who are spiritually blind, while it is life for those who see, reflecting Jesus' judgment in John 9:39.

In the same Gospel, John explains why many did not believe in Jesus by quoting Isaiah that God has blinded their eyes, confirming the theme that Jesus' coming reveals and intensifies existing blindness.
